summary: Trump indicated this week he plans to release UFO files in the "near future," while a congresswoman pledged to address information of "nonhuman origin," keeping pressure on the administration to follow through on disclosure promises. Meanwhile, several threads converged around missing scientists and UAP incidents: the parents of Chandra Levy connected their daughter's death to UFOs, former CIA and Defense officials weighed in on whether such cases hide deeper truths, and a UAP witness reportedly died of an overdose before testifying to Congress. Separately, unusual seismic activity near Area 51 sparked speculation from Harvard physicist Avi Loeb about government weapons testing, while investigative journalists flagged what they describe as a "CIA dirty secret" and questioned whether the Pentagon's UAP office can publicly speak the truth about what it knows. New archived documents covering UAP sightings from 2023 were added to the record, and Congress has until June 30 under FY2026 NDAA requirements to receive a classified UAP briefing.
